name: Fort Beauséjour
scope: The surviving five-bastion earth enclosure of Fort Beauséjour–Fort Cumberland and its outer ditch, named stone foundations and grass-covered powder magazine.
era: Standing archaeological site in the form documented by recent GeoNB airborne LiDAR and present mapped stonework.

externalReferences.title: A plan of the Fort of Beau Seiour with the attack in Iune 1755

originalReview.notes: Digitally inspected the full original plan, its manuscript date and credit, and native catalog entry. The 1756 plan is a faithful scan of mssHM 15424, created long before the copyright term. It corroborates the enclosure shape. Current LiDAR determines visible relief rather than historical levels.

review.method: Exactly matched public-domain originals, native building footprint and published architectural dimensions.
review.notes: Started with the published Qualla media. Its current exterior photo is attribution-licensed, and its separate historical map upload carries inconsistent authorship. The original 1756 plan deposited in the Huntington Library supplies verified public-domain imagery.
